lesson_title: Every Pea Was Once an Ovule
hook_text: Open a pea pod. Every single pea in there used to be a tiny part of a flower.
clip_script: A flower is a plant's way of having babies. Take one apart from the outside in. Green sepals: the jacket that protected the bud. Bright petals: the advertising, sometimes with markings only bees can see. Then the male parts, the stamens: a stick called the filament holding up the anther, a pollen factory. Every grain of pollen carries male cells. In the very centre, the female part, the carpel: a sticky stigma, the landing pad; a style, the neck; and the ovary, the nursery. Inside the ovary sit the ovules, each holding an egg cell. When pollen does its job, every ovule becomes a seed, and the ovary swells into a fruit. So a pea pod is an old ovary, and every pea was once an ovule.
visual_style: A whiteboard flower peeled ring by ring with labels popping up; a zoom into the ovary showing ovules that morph into peas inside a pod.
pacing: Steady ring-by-ring reveal, a quick zoom, a satisfying pea-pod ending.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and name every part of a flower.
